issues.title: Node execution started before being enqueued and marked as TAKEN
issues.description: The `start_execution` method is called before `enqueue_node`, which violates the expected state machine flow. The node is added to the `_executing_nodes` set before it's marked as TAKEN or added to the ready queue. This creates a race condition where concurrent operations might observe a node in the executing state while it's still in UNKNOWN state, leading to inconsistent state validation failures. The correct order should be: first enqueue (which marks as TAKEN and adds to queue), then start execution tracking.

issues.title: Edge marked as skipped after recursive propagation breaks skip chain
issues.description: In `_propagate_skip_to_node`, the edge is marked as skipped AFTER the recursive call to `propagate_skip_from_edge`. During the recursive propagation, the edge state is still UNKNOWN rather than SKIPPED. The `propagate_skip_from_edge` method analyzes incoming edge states and stops processing if any edge is UNKNOWN (line 56). This causes the skip propagation to terminate prematurely, leaving downstream nodes in an incorrect state instead of properly propagating the skip status through the entire dependency chain.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30251 - fix: workflow incorrectly marked as completed while nodes are still executing

structured_output.summary:
The PR targets a real race in the graph engine: when the last upstream node of a downstream node is skipped, `SkipPropagator.propagate_skip_from_edge` enqueues the downstream node via `enqueue_node` but never calls `start_execution`. Since `_executing_nodes` is empty and the ready queue drains, `is_execution_complete()` returns True while the node is still pending, so the dispatcher exits early. Adding `start_execution` in the `has_taken` branch matches the pattern used everywhere else in `event_handlers.py`, and that half of the fix is correct.

The PR also makes a second change that I verified is a regression. In `_propagate_skip_to_node`, the `mark_edge_skipped` call was moved to after the recursive `propagate_skip_from_edge`. `propagate_skip_from_edge` decides based on the incoming edges' states, so while the outgoing edge is still UNKNOWN, the downstream node sees `has_unknown` and returns early. With a chain `X -> B -> C` (plus a taken edge `T -> C`), the PR leaves `C` UNKNOWN, never enqueued, and the workflow completes without running it. I reproduced this by loading the real `GraphStateManager` and the PR's `SkipPropagator`: with the PR ordering, `C` ends in state `unknown` with an empty queue; with the original ordering, `C` is enqueued and started. The new unit tests don't catch it because they mock `analyze_edge_states` to return `all_skipped` unconditionally, so the recursive path is insensitive to edge ordering. The PR also leaves a debug `print` in the hot path."
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `start_execution` addition correctly fixes the reported bug. However, the reordering of `mark_edge_skipped` in `_propagate_skip_to_node` breaks multi-hop skip propagation: a downstream node that depends on a skipped chain is never enqueued or skipped, so the workflow can finish without running it. That is the same class of bug the PR is meant to fix, so it should be reverted before merge. The debug `print` and the weak test coverage should also be addressed.

architecture.overview:
The graph engine executes a workflow DAG with a `GraphStateManager` that tracks node/edge states (UNKNOWN/TAKEN/SKIPPED), a `ReadyQueue` of nodes to run, and a set of `_executing_nodes`. `GraphDispatcher._dispatcher_loop` treats the run as complete when the ready queue is empty and nothing is executing (`is_execution_complete`). When a node completes, `event_handlers.py` calls `enqueue_node` and `start_execution` together for every node it promotes. When a branch or upstream node is skipped, `SkipPropagator` walks the outgoing edges: if any incoming edge of a downstream node is TAKEN it enqueues the node, and if all are SKIPPED it marks the node skipped and recurses.

The PR changes this skip path in two ways. In the TAKEN branch it now calls `start_execution` before `enqueue_node`, which keeps `_executing_nodes` consistent with the ready queue, closing the window where the dispatcher could see an empty system. It also reorders the recursive walk in `_propagate_skip_to_node` so that the outgoing edge is marked SKIPPED after recursion instead of before. That reorder means the recursive call sees the edge as UNKNOWN, which stops propagation at the first hop. A debug `print` is also added and unit tests are added for the propagator.
steps: Entry point: `GraphDispatcher._dispatcher_loop` in `orchestration/dispatcher.py` keeps running while `ExecutionCoordinator.is_execution_complete()` is false, which in turn checks the ready queue and `_executing_nodes` in `GraphStateManager`.

Normal promotion: `event_handlers.py` (around lines 196-197, 279-280, 309-310) calls `enqueue_node` then `start_execution` for each ready node. The invariant is that every queued node is also tracked as executing.

Skip path: `SkipPropagator.propagate_skip_from_edge` inspects incoming edge states. The PR adds `start_execution` to the TAKEN branch so skip-triggered enqueues follow the same invariant. This is the correct part of the change.

Recursive skip: `_propagate_skip_to_node` marks a node skipped and then walks outgoing edges. The PR moves `mark_edge_skipped` after the recursive call, which leaves the edge UNKNOWN while its head is evaluated. That blocks propagation past the first hop, and this is the part that needs reverting.
Tests: the new `test_skip_propagator.py` mocks `GraphStateManager`, so it checks call shape but not state transitions. It does not exercise the multi-hop case that the reorder breaks.

findings.title: Reordered mark_edge_skipped stops multi-hop skip propagation
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/skip_propagator.py`, `_propagate_skip_to_node` (around lines 81-87) calls `propagate_skip_from_edge(edge.id)` before `mark_edge_skipped(edge.id)`. This is a regression: the downstream evaluation sees the edge as UNKNOWN and stops, so multi-hop skip chains never reach downstream nodes, and those nodes are never enqueued or skipped. Restore the original order: call `mark_edge_skipped(edge.id)` first, then `propagate_skip_from_edge(edge.id)`, matching `skip_branch_paths` (lines 95-97). Keep the `start_execution` addition in `propagate_skip_from_edge` as is. Then add a test using a real `GraphStateManager` with a chain X->B->C plus a taken T->C, and assert that C is enqueued and started.

findings.title: Unit tests mock state away and cannot detect the edge-ordering regression
findings.body:
The new tests replace `GraphStateManager` with `create_autospec`, and the recursion tests set `analyze_edge_states.return_value` to a fixed dict. Because the result doesn't depend on the real edge states, any ordering of `mark_edge_skipped` passes. `test_propagate_skip_from_edge_recursively_propagates_through_graph` (line 186) is the closest to the affected path, but it only checks `assert_any_call`, not ordering or the state seen during recursion. `test_propagate_skip_to_node_marks_node_and_outgoing_edges_skipped` (line 115) even says in its comments that the recursion can't be verified.

The taken-branch test (line 51) does assert `start_execution`, which is good. Still, the important behaviour here is state-dependent, so it needs a test that uses real edge state transitions.

::code{file="api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/test_skip_propagator.py" lines="186-200"}

Add a test that builds a small graph with real `Edge` states and a real `GraphStateManager`, covering: (a) a skipped chain X->B->C where C also has a taken incoming edge from T, asserting C ends TAKEN and is in the ready queue with `start_execution` recorded; (b) a fully skipped chain, asserting every downstream node ends SKIPPED. Both cases would have caught the reorder.
findings.fixPrompt: The unit tests in `api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/test_skip_propagator.py` mock `GraphStateManager` and fix `analyze_edge_states` to return `all_skipped`, so they can't detect edge-state ordering bugs in the recursive skip path (e.g. `_propagate_skip_to_node` in `skip_propagator.py`). Add at least one test that uses a real `GraphStateManager` and `ReadyQueue` with real `Edge` objects and state transitions. Cover a skipped chain X->B->C where C also has a taken edge from T (assert C is TAKEN, queued, and marked executing), and a fully skipped chain (assert all downstream nodes are SKIPPED). Keep the existing mock tests, but drop the 'We'll trust the logic' comment in `test_propagate_skip_to_node_marks_node_and_outgoing_edges_skipped`, since the new test covers it.

findings.title: Leftover debug print in the skip-propagation hot path
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/skip_propagator.py`, remove the debug `print(f"Starting execution for node: {downstream_node_id}")` line in `propagate_skip_from_edge` (around line 62). Keep the `start_execution(downstream_node_id)` and `enqueue_node(downstream_node_id)` calls that follow it. If a log line is useful, use the module's logger at debug level rather than `print`.

findings.title: Adding start_execution to the skip-triggered enqueue fixes the premature completion
findings.body:
This is the core of the fix. A node enqueued from the skip path was tracked only in the ready queue, so once the queue drained, `is_execution_complete()` returned true and the dispatcher exited while the node was still pending. Calling `start_execution` alongside `enqueue_node` matches the pattern already used in `event_handlers.py` (lines 196-197, 279-280, 309-310), so the skip path now follows the same invariant as the normal path. Because `_executing_nodes` is a set, a duplicate call is harmless.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/graph_engine/graph_traversal/skip_propagator.py" lines="59-66"}

findings.title: Test for the taken-edge enqueue path asserts the execution-tracking fix
findings.body: `test_propagate_skip_from_edge_with_taken_edge_enqueues_node` (line 51) asserts both `enqueue_node` and `start_execution` for the node. This pins the bug fix directly, so reverting the `start_execution` line would fail a test. The unknown-edge and all-skipped branches are also covered for their own calls.
